name: cracked asphalt road tile with a water-filled pothole and weeds, laid among plain asphalt
label: wasteland_ruins/asphalt-b

surfaces.part: asphalt ground with cracks (flat tile pattern)
water-filled potholes (dark openings with brown rims)

answer.evidence: The 64x48 image is a seamless ground texture of grey-blue asphalt with brown-grey crack patterns. It has no silhouette (width 64 on every row), no standing body and no front face. The potholes at about rows 5-12 and 21-28 are small dark pools with brown rims and a green weed tuft, all drawn flat on the ground plane. For a terrain tile this is the expected flat top-down surface, so there is no front elevation or side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 6 visible tones per tile. That sits between the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7), and it is well above the grass. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the asphalt has no flat fills. Speckle grain, crack lines and the dark pothole with weed pixels vary across the whole patch. Only 18% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark crack and pothole pixels lean toward the blue-grey and green of their neighbours. This is not a uniform black sticker outline. The ramp of about 5 steps (light speckle, mid grey-blue, dark grey, deep pothole, green weed) is slightly shallower than the paving reference's 6-7, and the raw palette is small at 14 colours. The visible tone count and texture still hold up against the references at the same scale. The weakest point is that the pothole reads as a dark blob and its water highlights are faint, but this is a minor craft issue and not a flat or sticker look.

surfaces.part: water-filled pothole (dark hole with brown edge and teal glint)

answer.evidence: The candidate is a full-bleed 64x48 ground texture with uniform width (0-47:64). It is a flat terrain surface of mottled grey-teal asphalt with brown-pink crack lines. The only features are two small pothole depressions with a dark opening, brown rim and teal water glint, plus green weeds. No standing volume, front-edge line, eave shadow or vertical south face is drawn, which is appropriate for a ground tile. The column scan shows a repeating pattern every 16 rows, so this is a tiling texture rather than a standing object.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's asphalt is a speckled blue-grey and rose-grey mix with 6 visible tones per tile. That is on par with the paving reference (7) and above the grass (3), and near-flat coverage is 0%. The speckle is fairly uniform noise, though, not shaded stones or per-tile highlights, so the ramp is only about 4 steps against the references' 5-6. The pothole is a tiny dark blob with a few green weed pixels; it is small and has no rim highlight, no water sheen ramp, and no crack structure to speak of. The cracks read as scattered dark dashes instead of connected, shaded fissures. Only 18% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the dark pixels carry a tint and avoid the black sticker look, but the pothole edge is a dark near-black clump, so the outline is mixed. Overall it is clean and not flat, but it is a thinner and less crafted piece than the paving reference. When in doubt, fail.
